answer: The velvet holds work receipts rather than names, so the cipher of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. The design leans on time-locked work history, revoked by a single upheld challenge, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. The timber of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit.
